issues.description: RevokeErr surfaced to API without sanitization may leak sensitive backend error text
issues.detail: The PR's own description flags this concern. RevokeErr is whatever the backend returned (DB driver messages, URLs, credentials in error strings). The handler now copies it straight through to the response. Either redact/truncate, gate behind a sudo capability, or document that backends must not put secrets in revoke errors. The data flow is right; the boundary check isn't.

issues.description: Rename FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo is a public API break with no compatibility shim
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes was an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming it forces every external caller to change. A two-line wrapper keeping the old name as a deprecated alias would cost nothing. Small composable tools shouldn't break their seams to add three fields.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport copies fields field-by-field; a small struct would make intent obvious
issues.detail: The function is now a hand-rolled projection of leaseEntry. Each new exported field requires editing this copy. Either define an explicit ExportedLeaseInfo struct (data structure, not algorithm) so the shape is the API, or accept that leaseEntry-as-DTO is the contract and document it. Right now it's the worst of both.

issues.description: Mixing t.Context() into one call site while leaving namespace.RootContext(nil) elsewhere is inconsistent
issues.detail: Line 2450 was changed to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()); the parallel test at line 3104 still uses namespace.RootContext(nil). Either change is fine, but doing one and not the other in the same diff is noise. Pick one shape for test contexts in this file.

issues.description: Test only asserts path; namespace_path and revoke_error paths are uncovered
issues.detail: The new test checks resp.Data["path"] but not the two other new fields or the conditional branches that gate them (empty namespace, empty RevokeErr). Three small assertions would cover the actual surface this PR adds. Data dominates; test the data.

review.summary: A small, well-shaped change: three fields added to a lookup response, plumbed through one projection function. The rename FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo is honest about the function's broader purpose but breaks an exported API without an alias. The real concern is the one the author already raised: RevokeErr is backend-supplied text being handed to clients with no sanitization or capability gate; that boundary needs a decision before merge. The projection function is starting to want to be an explicit DTO struct rather than a partial leaseEntry copy.
